title: Compose and index durable provider process observations
description: Prerequisite for task-ded026d6587442eabc28ff2609d231aa. Current measurement at HEAD a42ae2f: safe_boundary.observe is envelope-reachable, but there is no system-runner/host observation source a handler can trust. The existing production pieces `launchActivationProviderRun` -> `commitActivationProviderRun` -> `commitProviderRunRecord` correctly bind the physical launcher handoff and ProviderRunRef(attempt/effect/run/epoch), yet have zero non-test call sites and no strict reader selecting the run by attemptRef. FoundationAttemptRecorded drops exit state, and activation PROCESS_OBSERVED is registration rather than termination. Deliverable: compose the existing physical launch/commit chain at the real dispatch/reconciliation boundary and expose a decision-verified current provider-run observation reader by project+attempt. Consumer: task-ded026d6587442eabc28ff2609d231aa.
definitionOfDone: A production dispatch/reconciliation call site invokes exactly `launchActivationProviderRun` and then `commitActivationProviderRun`; the persisted ProviderRunRecord comes from the real launcher handoff, never from a safe_boundary.observe payload or a locally rebuilt observation.

The committed record retains the exact ProviderRunRef attemptRef/effectIntentId/runRef/epoch plus launcher exit/reconciliation truth, and is decision-backed to the authenticated project/session identity; a caller cannot select or rewrite any of those facts.

A strict current reader selects by projectId and attemptRef using an index-backed bounded scan, verifies command receipt/decision identity and canonical bytes, and returns exactly one record; ABSENT, UNREADABLE, MALFORMED, AMBIGUOUS and BINDING_MISMATCH have distinct stable codes and exact layers.

Real-Sqlite tests drive the production physical-boundary composition, cover one accepted observed-exit control plus unobserved, vanished, unreadable, duplicate, foreign-project and conflicting replay cases, and assert exact code/layer, zero partial residue, raw counts, and nonzero generated cases.
Exact replay returns the original record without a second physical launch or append; conflicting command bytes refuse before launch/commit and leave the original bytes unchanged.

Completion names task-ded026d6587442eabc28ff2609d231aa as consumer and records its exact reader call site; daemon typecheck/test and the existing plain-Node provider construction test execute with nonzero test evidence.
taskRails: Compose the existing public runner/daemon launch and provider-run ledger surfaces; do not add a wire kind, reimplement process observation, infer exit from FoundationAttemptRecorded, or treat PROCESS_OBSERVED registration as termination.
Only the physical launcher/reconciliation boundary may supply exit facts. Caller payloads may identify no run, exit, reconciliation, observation ref, or safe flag.
Verify every cross-package manifest/lock/bare-import edge before naming it; preserve upstream runner/ledger refusal code and layer rather than restamping.
Use real SqliteEventStore, TDD exact codes/layers, bounded index reads, target <=250 lines per production source, and explicit owned-path commits.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED — PORTABLE COMPOSITION, IDENTITY, AND CALLER-AUTHORITY FENCE in `foundation-attempt-service.test.ts`, over a real file-backed `SqliteEventStore`. Pin the durable `ProviderRunRef` exactly to `{provider:"claude",runRef:deriveDispatchAggregateId(activationAggregateId),effectIntentId:"intent-1",attemptRef:"attempt-1",epoch:3}`, the returned session to the lease `ownerSessionRef` (deliberately different from the activation principal), launch `REFUSED`, terminal `REFUSED`, infrastructure `LAUNCH_REFUSED`, upstream `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED@TELEMETRY_LAUNCH`, null daemon clock observations, one provider event, and one `provider-run.telemetry.commit` decision whose project and principal are the durable project and lease session. THE COMPOSITION TEST, over the real SqliteEventStore, the real activation ingress and the REAL launcher's own non-Windows refusal (a BLIND handoff: ok:true carrying UNKNOWN facts — the arm a happy-path-only composition drops):
- Foundation's own answer must stay CLAUDE_LAUNCH_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED@LAUNCHER — composing the provider run may not restamp the launcher's refusal.
- Every provider fact is read back through the SHIPPED `readCurrentProviderRun`, never off dispatch's return value: the claim is that a durable decision-verified run exists, and a return value cannot say that.
- providerRunRef pinned FIELD BY FIELD to { provider:"claude", runRef: DISPATCH_AGGREGATE (deriveDispatchAggregateId of the activation aggregate), effectIntentId:"intent-1", attemptRef:"attempt-1", epoch:3 } — all server-derived, none caller-supplied.
- THE GOVERNOR'S PIN (comment-132336517) made executable: `read.sessionId` must be SESSION_ID, and the test also asserts SESSION_ID !== PRINCIPAL_ID. The fixture's lease owner and envelope principal are deliberately different values, so a writer keying the provider decision to the envelope principal commits successfully and then the reader refuses PROVIDER_RUN_BINDING_MISMATCH — the failure mode that "masquerades as a reader defect". This assertion is what turns that into a named red.
- The blind-arm facts, from the landed commit suite's own vocabulary: launch.kind REFUSED, terminal REFUSED, infrastructure LAUNCH_REFUSED, upstreamRefusal TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED@TELEMETRY_LAUNCH.
- observedStart and observedEnd both null — there is no daemon boot/monotonic observation to read, and inventing one from the launcher's wall stamps would be a second clock.
- EXACTLY ONE physical composition: one PROVIDER_RUN_EVENT_TYPE event and one provider-run.telemetry.commit decision, the decision keyed to projectId PROJECT_ID and principalId SESSION_ID.

THE CALLER-AUTHORITY FENCE, 14 generated arms plus a positive control on the generator ("generated a nonempty smuggling sweep"): providerRun, providerRunRef, runRef, epoch, exit, reconciliation, terminal, infrastructure, observation, safeBoundaryObserved, launcher, launch, deps, clock. Each is smuggled as an extra top-level request field; each must refuse FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REQUEST_MALFORMED@DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT and leave zero provider events, zero provider decisions, zero activation events and zero dispatch events.

Those 14 arms pass ALREADY, and that is the honest reading: `decodeFoundationAttemptRequest` uses exactKeys on the outer request, so the fence exists today. They are here as the regression guard for step 5 — the danger is that wiring the provider run introduces a field the decoder starts tolerating. Recording that they were green before the production change so nobody later reads them as evidence the change created the fence.

A materially changed `cwd` or other identity-covered command byte under the same dispatch aggregate must refuse `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REPLAY_MISMATCH@DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT` before adapter or provider commit, preserving the original provider bytes/digest. Reuse the existing real-store aborting wrapper at provider commit ordinal 4: assert `PROVIDER_RUN_STORE_UNAVAILABLE@PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER` (and the exact storeCode shape production returns), zero provider event/decision residue, no false reader authority, and no second physical attempt. Querying the accepted record under a foreign project must preserve `PROVIDER_RUN_BINDING_MISMATCH@PROVIDER_RUN_READER` and change no counts. Do not duplicate the landed 64-case reader matrix: explicitly retain its real-SQLite ABSENT, RECORD_UNREADABLE, EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE, cross-page AMBIGUOUS, foreign binding, bounded-scan, positive generated-count, and zero-write assertions as prerequisite coverage run in the final focused gate.
implementationPlan.note:
FOUR MORE RED, all for the same missing composition. `Tests 5 failed | 45 passed (50)` in this file, up from 46 tests after step 2. Every red names a provider-boundary behaviour that does not exist yet; nothing pre-existing moved.

THE SNAPSHOT the replay cases compare, taken through the SHIPPED reader plus the store itself: provider event count, provider decision count, the reader's own recordDigest, and the whole-store event horizon. Counts AND bytes together, because a re-commit that happened to produce identical bytes would still move the counts, and a count check alone cannot see a rewritten record.

RED 2, "replays without launching, committing or moving a single provider byte": first dispatch, snapshot (events must be exactly 1), second identical dispatch. The replay must adopt the stored Foundation record and the whole snapshot must be byte-for-byte equal afterwards. A second physical launch is the single worst defect this task can introduce, and the provider ledger is where it shows up.

RED 3, "refuses a drifted command before the provider boundary and preserves the run": same dispatch aggregate, `cwd` changed to D:/other-worktree. Must refuse FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REPLAY_MISMATCH@DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT — the reservation fence answering BEFORE any authority, adapter or provider commit — with the snapshot unchanged.

RED 4, "keeps the provider ledger's own refusal when the provider commit aborts": the existing real-store aborting proxy at commit ORDINAL 4. The ordinal is documented in the test the way its sibling documents ordinal 3: one dispatch commits (1) the activation ledger record, (2) the durable attempt-resource set, (3) the Foundation reservation, (4) the provider-run commit. Asserts injected.fired() === 1, then PROVIDER_RUN_STORE_UNAVAILABLE@PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER preserved rather than restamped as a Foundation code, zero provider events, zero provider decisions, and — the part a count check cannot say — the reader still answers PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_ABSENT, so no false authority survives the abort.

RED 5, "refuses a foreign project against an accepted record and changes no counts": PROVIDER_RUN_BINDING_MISMATCH@PROVIDER_RUN_READER with the snapshot unchanged. The project gate answers before a page is read, so this also proves the accepted record is not visible cross-project.

NOT DUPLICATED, deliberately: the landed 64-case reader matrix (provider-run-reader.test.ts) already covers ABSENT, RECORD_UNREADABLE, EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE, the cross-page AMBIGUOUS duplicate, foreign binding, the bounded scan, its positive generated-count control and its zero-write assertions. Re-implementing those here would be a second, drifting copy; they are retained as prerequisite coverage and run in the final focused gate as one of the five files.

One correction to the plan's wording, recorded so QA does not read it as a miss: step 3 asks for "the transparent adapter/commit totals at one". I am asserting the DURABLE totals — provider events, provider decisions, reader digest, store horizon — rather than in-process call counters. The durable ledger is the stronger statement (a wrapper counter proves a function was called; the ledger proves what was written), and it does not require module mocking to observe. The one-call property is additionally pinned by the landed adapter suite, which owns that assertion.

THE OBSERVED PHYSICAL CONTROL IS RED FOR THE RIGHT REASON, and getting there disproved the suite's own stale premise.

RUN: `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests 1 failed | 3 passed (4)`. The single red is "foundation attempt dispatch — the observed physical control > observes a real exited provider process and files it in the ledger", failing at line 463 on `expect(read).toMatchObject({ ok: true })` with `+ "ok": false` — the SHIPPED reader, refusing because nothing committed a provider run. Everything before that assertion passed, and the case took 5565ms: a real Claude child process was started, ran `--version`, exited on its own, and the Foundation dispatch answered ok.

THE STALE PREMISE, now measured rather than repeated. The existing suite's header says "no case here reaches PROVEN: the public surface withholds observeInstalledClaudeRuntime, probeClaudeRuntime and capabilitySchemaDigestOf, so NO consumer can mint a quote production would accept". That is no longer true: `discoverInstalledClaudeRuntime()` (packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-runtime-discovery.ts:160) is public, takes NO argument, and mints the quote itself — it resolves the installed executable from the host's own configuration, refuses zero candidates and refuses more than one, and calls `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` at the only permitted call site. Because it takes no parameter, a test cannot steer it, which is exactly why it is safe to build a control on. My step-1 bare-specifier probe already proved it is reachable from apps/daemon as an @moe/runner export (a root-barrel grep misses it — the index re-exports with `export *`).

THE CONTROL, with no dynamic skip: on a Windows host, discovery refusing is an explicit THROW naming the refusal JSON, not an `it.skip`. A missing prerequisite must be a red; skipping is how a suite quietly stops proving its own subject.

WHAT IT ASSERTS once the composition lands: the durable ProviderRunRef field by field ({provider:"claude", runRef: DISPATCH_AGGREGATE, effectIntentId:"intent-1", attemptRef:"attempt-1", epoch:3}), sessionId === SESSION_ID with SESSION_ID !== PRINCIPAL_ID, launch.kind OBSERVED, launch.exit { kind:"EXITED", code:0 }, upstreamRefusal null, the record frozen, exactly one provider event and one provider decision, and `existsSync(pinRoot)` true — the runner's pinned copy is its first physical act, so the pin root existing is evidence the boundary was reached rather than short-circuited.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM, stated in the test: `--version` proves a real process started, exited on its own and was observed. It is NOT a completed provider result, and nothing reads it as one.

REPLAY AND CONFLICT, in the same case so they run against the SAME durable state: an exact replay must leave provider events at 1, provider decisions at 1, the activation event list identical and the reader's recordDigest unchanged; then one identity-covered byte (`cwd`) must refuse FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_REPLAY_MISMATCH@DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT with the provider row still at 1. Store closed before the temp root is removed — a held SQLite handle throws EPERM on Windows cleanup and kills the worker with no output.

The three pre-existing Windows cases (unproven runtime, reservation abort, self-assembled quote for the real installed Claude) are untouched and still pass with their exact codes and layers.

The edda1fd3 reader enforces principal==ownerSessionRef and will refuse every record with PROVIDER_RUN_BINDING_MISMATCH otherwise — correct fail-closed behavior that will masquerade as a reader defect to whoever hits it first. A mutation drill in edda1fd3's plan proves the check is load-bearing. Also inherit these traps: (1) duplicate-detection tests must seed duplicates ACROSS a page boundary — a first-match reader passes single-page seeds with the defect intact; (2) re-derive the aggregate id from the DECODED providerRunRef, never from the event's own stored fields (self-comparison; provider-run-contracts.ts header warns readers must compare rather than trust hash uniqueness); (3) CommandDecisionRecord is a union and NoBusinessEffectDecision carries NULL versions — discriminate on effectDisposition BEFORE any previousVersion === 0 check, since null === 0 is silently false.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Keep `createFoundationClaudeLauncher` and append telemetry afterward: rejected because that either launches twice or fabricates a handoff from a raw result. 2) Replace it with raw `launchClaudeWithTelemetry`: rejected because it bypasses the durable grant/process-registration authority. 3) Rebuild/spread `{result,handoff}` in the daemon: rejected because only the runner witnessed that they came from one capture; the adapter deliberately returns the pair by identity. 4) Use the authenticated envelope principal for the provider decision: rejected because the landed current reader requires the attempt lease's `ownerSessionRef`, deliberately distinct in real fixtures. 5) Infer clock observations from launcher ISO timestamps or use wall time: rejected; provider wall truth stays in the handoff and no boot/monotonic observation exists. 6) Persist `FoundationAttemptRecorded`/`PROCESS_OBSERVED` as exit truth: rejected by task rail; neither is physical terminal evidence. 7) Call `readCurrentProviderRun` inside the service as a second availability gate: rejected; commit already returns the durable result, tests certify the reader, and downstream task-ded026 is its real production consumer. 8) Extend the DONE reader/adapter/ledger tests or add a helper module: rejected; prerequisites already own those surfaces and the final slice is intentionally three files. 9) Treat reader failure after a successful provider commit as zero-residue: rejected as a false atomicity claim; postcommit evidence must survive, while zero residue is asserted only before commit.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured on moving shared-tree HEADs f96995d then d496b5e. All six prerequisites are on disk. `foundation-attempt-service.ts` is 248 lines; it currently wins RESERVED/replay fencing before an 8-line raw `createFoundationClaudeLauncher` block and then passes that raw result to `readDurableFoundationObservation`. `launchActivationProviderRun` is 143 lines, requires a separate authority, invokes public `createTelemetryBoundClaudeLauncher` once, and returns the exact `ClaudeBoundLaunchResult`. `commitActivationProviderRun` is 249 lines and commits the handoff-derived record; `readCurrentProviderRun` is 249 lines and joins the provider decision to the activation by project+attempt, verifying effect, lease epoch, and `decision.key.principalId === ownerSessionRef`. The reader suite already executes 64 real-SQLite cases including accepted, ABSENT, canonical unreadable, store unreadable, foreign binding, and a duplicate deliberately beyond the first indexed page. Provider commit and adapter suites add 16 and 34 production-surface cases. Combined current focused baseline was 5 files / 147 tests; service+Windows+reader was independently 3 files / 97 tests; daemon typecheck was exit 0 at a clean snapshot. `apps/daemon` declares both runner/store workspace dependencies and the lock importer links them. Public `discoverInstalledClaudeRuntime()` returned PROVEN on this Windows host for Claude 2.1.234, and a harmless installed `--version --model ... --effort high` invocation exited 0. Full daemon red observed during planning was foreign bridge/registry WIP outside all three owned paths; the worker must take a fresh merge-base baseline because HEAD is moving.
planningNotes.risks: The highest-risk defect is a second physical launch on replay or while trying to recover a raw result; the transparent adapter counter, provider counts, and landed adapter one-call proof must all agree. A provider decision keyed to the envelope principal will commit successfully but the strict reader will correctly refuse it as a foreign session. `identity.bytes`, reservation bytes, decision request SHA, event request SHA, and effect SHA are distinct domains; do not substitute one because lengths/digests look plausible. Blind/refused launches are valid durable UNKNOWN evidence and must be committed; they are not accepted physical exits. Conversely, `--version` proves an observed EXITED process but not a completed provider result. An unexpected adapter throw may become only the existing `FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT_LAUNCH_UNKNOWN@DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT`; never let it escape as a crash. The provider-commit abort occurs after activation and Foundation reservation, so zero residue is scoped to provider rows/decisions and physical invocation, not a rollback of already-authoritative activation/reservation facts. Current reader availability failures after a commit cannot erase the committed provider record. Windows handles/store must close before cleanup. Service has only two lines of target headroom, so replace and compact; do not grow DONE 249-line producers. Shared-tree baselines are volatile: no broad restore/stage/commit and no attribution of foreign registry/context work to this task.
